free_tier.stated: Starter: 2 GB serverless storage, 5 indexes, 1 project, 1 GB egress per month, us-east-1 only

per_object_cap.stated: 2 GB of index storage per organization; 100 namespaces per index

retention.stated: an index persists while the plan is active; no deletion clock is published for Starter

egress.terms: 1 GB per month on Starter. Builder is 10 GB; Standard includes 100 GB then USD 0.10/GB

interface_detail: a REST API for data and control planes; Python, Node and Java SDKs; the pinecone CLI
tooling: the Pinecone SDKs and CLI; no Postgres extension path
chaining: a free vector index that mostly matters for a workload too large for pgvector on a free Postgres, because pgvector is already available on both Neon and Supabase at no extra cost

limits.value: 2 GB of storage per organization, not per index
1 GB egress per month on Starter
5 indexes, 1 project per organization, us-east-1 only, and 100 namespaces per index
no connection limit is published for Starter; recorded as a gap

identity_cost.detail: email signup; no card on Starter

confidence_note: the pricing comparison table was read today. The 1 GB monthly egress is on it and was not in the census. the pricing page states them and is now the only source for them.

evidence.proved: Starter: storage up to 2 GB, egress up to 1 GB/month, indexes up to 5, namespaces per index 100; Builder USD 25 with 10 GB storage and 10 GB egress; Standard unlimited at USD 0.33/GB-month

notes: 2 GB is an organization-level cap and one project is the whole allowance, so there is no way to shard around it. 1 GB a month of egress is 33 MB a day, which a retrieval workload serving embeddings exceeds before the 2 GB of storage matters.
